quote: Example 3.1. Let X be a nonnegative random variable with density function f(x) = (x² + c)e^{−x}/(c + 2). ... By choosing c ∈ (0, 2) we obtain rX,1 that starts decreasing and eventually becomes increasing, while rX,2 is increasing. That is, X is not 1−IFR but is 2−IFR. Moreover, it is also easy to verify that X is not 1−IFRA.
compared: iterated failure-rate monotonicity classes of a single distribution

conclusion.direction: X not 1-IFR but 2-IFR; also not 1-IFRA — supports Corollary 3.1 (s-IFRA monotonicity not hereditary)

ambiguity: Single-distribution ageing-class example, included because it is the printed example supporting the ordering-related Corollary 3.1.

quote: Proposition 3.1. Let Y1 and Y2 be independent exponential random variables with mean 1 and 1/λ, respectively, where λ ≠ 1, and define Y = max(Y1, Y2). Then Y is 1−IFRA, but it is neither 2−IFRA nor 2−DFRA. Moreover, there exists s0 > 2 such that Y is s−DFR for every s ≥ s0.
family: Y = max(Y1, Y2), Y1 ~ Exp(1), Y2 ~ Exp(λ), λ ≠ 1
compared: ageing monotonicity classes of Y (equivalently, order comparisons of Y against the exponential)

hypotheses.text: λ ≠ 1; components independent exponentials with means 1 and 1/λ

conclusion.direction: Y is 1-IFRA but neither 2-IFRA nor 2-DFRA, and is s-DFR for all s >= some s0 > 2

ambiguity: Class-membership claim rather than a pairwise ordering; via Theorem 2.1 it is equivalent to ordering comparisons vs exponential variables.

quote: Corollary 3.1. The s−IFRA monotonicity does not have the hereditary property.
family: general nonnegative distributions; Example 3.1 and Proposition 3.1 as witnesses
compared: s-IFRA class membership across iteration levels

quote: Proposition 5.1. Let X be a random variable with distribution function FX ∈ F and Y a random variable with exponential distribution. Then X ≤2−IFR Y if and only if X ≤DMRL Y.
compared: equivalence of 2-IFR and DMRL orders against an exponential reference

quote: Corollary 5.1. Let X be a random variable with distribution function FX ∈ F and Y a random variable with exponential distribution. If, for some s ≥ 1, X ≤s−IFR Y, then X ≤(s+1)−IFR Y.
compared: heredity of s-IFR ordering against exponential reference

quote: Proposition 5.2. Neither the 1−IFR or the DMRL order imply the 2−IFR order. ... A possible choice is X ∼ BP(5, 10) and Y ∼ BP(2, 6). For these parameters, we find d(x) = ... that is decreasing, c2′(x) = ... which is not monotone, and c1(x) = TY,1(TX,1^{−1})(x) = ... which is convex.
family: branched Pareto BP(c1, c2): T X,1(x) = c1²/(x+c1)² I[0,c1](x) + (c1+c2)²/(4(x+c2)²) I(c1,∞)(x)
compared: X ~ BP(5,10) vs Y ~ BP(2,6): 1-IFR and DMRL hold but 2-IFR fails

conclusion.direction: X <=1-IFR Y (c1 convex) and X <=DMRL Y (d decreasing), but not X <=2-IFR Y (c2′ non-monotone)

quote: Proposition 6.1. If α > 1, then Weibull(α, θ1) ≤s−IFR Γ(α, θ2), for every s ≥ 1.
family: Weibull(α, θ) vs Gamma Γ(α, θ) (scale parameters immaterial)
compared: Weibull vs Gamma with common shape α > 1

conclusion.direction: Weibull(α, θ1) <=s-IFR Γ(α, θ2) for every s >= 1

quote: Theorem 6.2. Let α′ > α > 0. 1. If X ∼ Γ(α′, θ1) and Y ∼ Γ(α, θ2) then X ≤s−IFR Y. 2. If X ∼ Weibull(α′, θ1) and Y ∼ Weibull(α, θ2) then X ≤s−IFR Y.
model: two single random variables within one family
compared: same-family distributions with ordered shape parameters

conclusion.direction: (1) Γ(α′, θ1) <=s-IFR Γ(α, θ2); (2) Weibull(α′, θ1) <=s-IFR Weibull(α, θ2) for all s >= 1

ambiguity: Case 1 > α′ > α > 0 proved here; remaining cases from Propositions 30-33 of Arab and Oliveira.

quote: Proposition 7.1. Let X and Y be defined as in (7.1) [X = max(X1, X2), X1, X2 iid mean-1 exponentials; Y = max(Y1, Y2), Y1 ~ Exp(1), Y2 ~ Exp(mean 1/λ < 1)]. For every s ≥ 1 and x ≥ 0, we have TX,s(x) ≥ TY,s(x).
family: max of iid Exp(1) pair vs max of Exp(1) and Exp(λ) (λ > 1) pair
compared: s-iterated tails of X and Y

conclusion.direction: TX,s(x) >= TY,s(x) for all x, s — the s-iterate of X is stochastically larger than the s-iterate of Y

ambiguity: λ > 1 assumed in the proof; (7.1) says mean of Y2 is 1/λ < 1.

quote: Corollary 7.1. Let X and Y be defined as in (7.1). Then TY,s(TX,s^{−1}(x))/x ≤ 1, for every x > 0.
Proposition 7.2. Let X and Y be defined as in (7.1). For every s ≥ 1, X ≤s−IFRA Y.
family: max of iid Exp(1) vs max of Exp(1) and Exp(λ)
compared: s-IFRA ordering of the two maxima

quote: Theorem 7.1. Let X and Y be defined as in (7.1). For every s ≥ 1, X ≤s−IFR Y.
family: max of iid Exp(1) vs max of Exp(1) and Exp(λ)
compared: iterated failure-rate ordering of homogeneous vs heterogeneous two-component parallel systems

conclusion.direction: X <=s-IFR Y for every s >= 1 (homogeneous system ages faster in s-IFR sense)

ambiguity: Only n = 2 systems treated; the n-component generalization is open (Remark 7.1-7.2).

quote: Proposition 7.3. Let X1, . . . , Xm, m ≥ 3, be independent random variables with exponential distribution with mean 1/λ, and Y1, . . . , Yk, 2 ≤ k < m, independent exponential random variables with mean 1/β. If X(m) = max(X1, . . . , Xm) and Y(k) = max(Y1, . . . , Yk), then X(m) ≤1−IFR Y(k).
family: iid exponential components (means 1/λ and 1/β; scale-free so λ = β = 1 w.l.o.g.)
compared: max of m iid exponentials vs max of k < m iid exponentials

conclusion.direction: X(m) <=1-IFR Y(k) (larger system is smaller in 1-IFR order)

quote: Corollary 7.2. Let X1, . . . , Xn, n ≥ 3, be independent random variables with exponential distribution with mean 1/λ, and define, for each k = 2, . . . , n, X(k) = max(X1, . . . , Xk). Then X(n) ≤1−IFR X(n−1) ≤1−IFR ··· ≤1−IFR X(2).
compared: maxima over subsets of decreasing size

quote: Write, for simplicity, X = max{X1, X2} and Y = max{Y1, Y2} and consider Vs(x) = TY,s(x) − TX,s(ax), where a > 0. If we choose the parameters (s, λ1/λ2, θ1/θ2, a) = (2, 0.34, 11, 2.89) the sign variation of Vs(x) is “−, +, −” so, according to Theorem 2.2, X and Y are not comparable with respect to the 2−IFRA order, hence they cannot be comparable with respect to the 2−IFR order. ... (λ1, λ2, θ1, θ2) = (1/1474)(408, 1200, 134, 1474)ϑ, with ϑ > 0, generates a whole family of counter-examples for the conjecture when the iteration parameter s = 2.
model: parallel systems of two exponentials with majorized rate vectors
family: max of two exponentials, rates (λ1, λ2) ≺ (θ1, θ2)
compared: X vs Y under component-rate majorization (Kochar–Xu conjecture stated for 1-IFR)

conclusion.direction: Vs has sign variation '−, +, −' — X and Y not comparable in 2-IFRA, hence not in 2-IFR, refuting the iterated-order extension of the Kochar–Xu conjecture

ambiguity: The s = 1 conjecture itself remains unresolved (no proof or counterexample found).
